info.title: kelve’s shared graph
info.description: The shared knowledge graph every kelve reads ideas and entries from, and adds them to. It holds general knowledge only: never anyone's work. Everything in it is public domain, under CC0 1.0, the graph as a database included; this API's own code is Apache-2.0. Reading and adding are for someone signed in, with GitHub or Google: a person's kelve gets an account key by signing in, has the graph sign a batch of reading tokens with it, blind, and spends one on each read: the graph knows a token is one it signed, never whose (Privacy Pass's privately verifiable tokens, RFC 9578, on the VOPRF of RFC 9497). Errors are RFC 9457 problem details.

get.summary: What the graph is.

The account the key is for: the name the graph made up for them, and
the version of the terms they agreed to.

delete.summary:
Deletes the account the key is for: the graph forgets who they are,
stops all their keys, withdraws ideas only they added and rejects their
waiting entries. What others can already read stays, under the handle
the graph made up.

get.summary: What the account has added, and how many times its entries were served.

post.summary:
Signs a batch of blinded reading tokens for the account, at most 100, as
many as it may have today, with a proof they were signed with the key
shown everyone. The graph never sees the tokens, so it can't tell later
whose one is.

429.description: As many as the account may have today: Retry-After says when there are more.

post.summary:
A reader's word that an entry didn't help them understand: it needs an
example, it's too hard, or something's missing. Kept with the idea, with
no account and no address, until a revision answers it.

422.description: Not an ask the graph can take.

get.summary: What became public, in order, for mirrors.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The `next` of the last page read.

401.description: Not signed in: read with a reading token, or an account’s key.

post.summary:
Adds ideas and entries, and proposes relations and taking them back.
Each change is taken or refused on its own; what's refused comes back in
`skipped`, with why. A relation must have a why: one plain sentence,
at most 200 characters, saying what one idea takes from the other. "Rests
on" is for what someone must understand first, at most three an idea,
most needed first; the problem an idea exists for is "answers"; a broader
category is "kind of". Relations are reviewed before they're served. The
same Idempotency-Key always gets the first answer, so a retry is applied
once.

401.description: No key, or one the graph doesn't know.

429.description: Over a limit: Retry-After says when to try again, in seconds. Titled "Too many requests", it's a few seconds. Titled "Enough for today", the account has added as many ideas, entries or relations as it may in a day, as the detail says, and "as a new account" while it's a new account's limit: Retry-After is the seconds to midnight UTC, when it resets.

503.description: Not taking changes for now: Retry-After says when to try again.

post.summary:
A week's counts, which a person chose to share: with the install's random
ID, and never an account, a key or a reading token.

get.summary: An idea's current entry: a redirect to its revision.

401.description: Not signed in: read with a reading token, or an account’s key.

get.summary: One revision of an entry. It never changes, and is cached for a year.

401.description: Not signed in: read with a reading token, or an account’s key.

post.summary:
A reader's word that an entry, a link in it, or a relation is wrong.
The graph's models check it again; no account is needed.

422.description: Not a flag the graph can take.

post.summary:
Relations readers followed, from one idea's entry to an idea it relates
to: one more for each. No account, and nothing about who sent them,
which project or file, or when. The graph orders each idea's relations,
within each kind, by how often they're followed.

get.summary: The ground floor: every idea that's a first principle.
Live ideas by ID, following merges.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: Up to 100 IDs, separated by commas.

401.description: Not signed in: read with a reading token, or an account’s key.

get.summary: One idea.

401.description: Not signed in: read with a reading token, or an account’s key.

get.summary:
What a person's agent is told to do for one kind of job: `read`,
`choose`, `builtOn`, `relate`, `write`, `fix`, `extend`,
`folders`, `note`, `plainly`, `plainlyFolder` or `plainlyChange`. The
graph serves them, so they improve for everyone at once.

The live lessons about some ideas, best first: what people's agents
learned using them. Each with what came of it for projects besides its
author's, and how far it's confirmed.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: Up to 100 idea IDs, separated by commas.

401.description: Not signed in: read with a reading token, or an account’s key.

post.summary:
Adds a lesson. It's checked in code at once, then by the graph's
models; it's live, not confirmed yet, once they pass it. One that says
what a lesson already there says isn't kept again: it's answered as
`same`, and counted as confirming that one. The same Idempotency-Key
always gets the first answer.

401.description: No key, or one the graph doesn't know.

422.description: The lesson isn't one the graph takes, as the detail says.

429.description: Over a limit, as for changesets: "as many lessons".

post.summary:
What came of lessons an agent was given: held, didn't, or not known,
and what showed it. Counted once a lesson for each account, and never
for its author's. Nothing else goes with it: never the problem, the
command or the file.

get.summary:
One lesson: live or the same as one, to anyone; in any other state,
only to its author's key. Anyone else is told there's no such lesson.

401.description: Not signed in: read with a reading token, or an account’s key.

post.summary:
The ideas each name may be, in the shape of the W3C Reconciliation API.
Names go only in the body, so they reach no log.

200.description: Candidates for each query, by the asker's own keys.

401.description: Not signed in: read with a reading token, or an account’s key.

429.description: Too many lookups: wait as Retry-After says.

get.summary:
One bucket of the name index: every live idea's name whose hash starts
with `prefix`, keyed by the whole hash. A kelve finds its own name in
it, so the graph never learns which name was asked.

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.description: The first four hex characters of the SHA-256 of the name, as names are compared.

401.description: Not signed in: read with a reading token, or an account’s key.

get.summary:
How ideas relate, both ways: for each, what it rests on (most needed
first), what it's a kind of, what it answers, its alternatives, what it's
used with, what rests on it, and the first principles it comes down to.
Only live and settled relations are served.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: Up to 50 idea IDs, separated by commas.

401.description: Not signed in: read with a reading token, or an account’s key.

get.summary: What rests on an idea, a page at a time, most read first.

401.description: Not signed in: read with a reading token, or an account’s key.

get.summary:
How the graph's check of an entry stands, for the account that wrote
it: claim by claim, as each is checked against its pages.

A person's kelve starts signing in: the browser goes on to GitHub, or
Google, and comes back to `redirect_uri` with a one-time code and
`state`. Either only tells the graph who someone is: it keeps a number
for the account (GitHub's id, Google's `sub`), never a name or email.

parameters.name: redirect_uri
parameters.description: http, to 127.0.0.1, [::1] or localhost, on a port (RFC 8252).

503.description: That way of signing in isn't set up on this graph: a page saying so.

delete.summary: Signs out: the key it's sent with stops working.

get.summary: Where GitHub sends the person back.

303.description: Back to the person's kelve, with `code` and `state`, or `error=access_denied`.

get.summary: Where Google sends the browser back to, after someone signs in there.

303.description: Back to kelve's redirect_uri, with a one-time code and state.

post.summary:
Exchanges a sign-in's one-time code, with its PKCE verifier, for a key
of this kelve's own. A code is taken once, within two minutes.

get.summary: What a person agrees to before anything they add goes into the graph.

post.summary:
Agrees to the terms, by their version. The graph takes nothing from an
account that hasn't agreed to the terms as they are now.

409.description: Not the terms as they are now.

get.summary:
The key the graph signs reading tokens with, the same for everyone:
asked for with no account, so it can't be one account's alone.

Account.description: The person's account, as the graph knows it.

agreed.description: The version of the terms they agreed to, if any.

handle.description: The name the graph made up for them.

Added.description: What an account has added, and how often others read it.

entries.description: Entries it added that the graph serves.

reads.description:
How many times its entries were served: close to one a reader,
since each kelve keeps an entry once it has it.

relations.description: Ways ideas relate it added that the graph serves.

Agree.description: Agreeing to a version of the terms.

entries.description:
Each entry written, by idea ID: its new revision. An entry stays
pending, seen only by the account that wrote it, until the graph's
own checks pass.

relations.description:
Each relation taken, and where it stands: proposed, until it's
reviewed.

skipped.description: What it left out, and why, in sentences.

Ask.description:
A reader's word that an entry didn't help them understand, and what it
needs. Like a flag, it carries nothing of who sent it, and nothing of their
work: the revision they read, and one of three words.

revision.description: The entry's revision, as the reader saw it.

AskKind.description: What readers, or the graph's own grade, ask an entry to add.

Backing.description: A public page that backs a lesson, and the line on it that does.

value.description: From 0 to 100, how long the bar is.

Block.description: One block of an entry: one of kelve's components.

oneOf.description:
The fold it's in, under its part, closed until the reader opens it.
None for a block that's always shown. Blocks in a row with the same
part and fold are one fold.

id.description:
Unique within its entry, and kept from one revision to the next:
`b1`, `b2`. A block added later gets an id no block had.

oneOf.description:
The part of the entry it's in. None in an entry written before
entries had parts.
A paragraph of two or three sentences. `quiet` for an aside.
A heading for a longer entry: a statement, never a label.
Bullets, only where something is a list.

Lines of the real thing: a change, a file, a message, a clause.
kelve copies the text in from what it heard; the model only says
which lines and which to mark.

lang.description:
What it's written in, as kelve tells from what it quoted: a
language in `code::LANGUAGES`, `prose`, or none for plain output.

oneOf.description:
A system, a process, a cycle, a timeline: drawn by kelve. With
steps, it plays through them once and rests on the last.

describe.description:
The diagram in words, for anyone who can't see it, and shown
under it.

oneOf.description: Your own numbers, to move: a formula kelve knows, with inputs.

output.description: What the result is, in words: "Monthly payment".

oneOf.description: Bars, for a few numbers side by side.
A small table. `marks` are `[row, column]` cells kelve's red marks.
Two approaches, or two options, side by side.
Short lines, each with a square: red for the one that matters.
When things happened.
Whoever you'd have to convince, and what they'd say.
"So if anyone asks…": one sentence you can use.

Who says what to whom, in order: people, programs or parts, each
message an arrow from one to another, drawn in turn.
A process to walk through a stage at a time, at the reader's pace.
Things placed on two axes, each from 0 to 100.
Where things sit between two ends, from 0 to 100.
A line or two over time, drawn as you reach it.

labels.description: Along the bottom, one for each value: "2018", "2020".

oneOf.description: A decision that branches, from one question at the top.
Two versions of a thing, to drag between.
One number, what it means, and where it's from.

share.description: How much of the whole it is, from 0 to 100, drawn as a bar.

oneOf.description:
Lines of the real thing, with notes pinned to the ones that matter.
kelve copies the lines in, as for an excerpt.
How many make it through each stage, from the first.

Bucket.description:
One bucket of the name index: every live idea's name whose hash starts
with the bucket's prefix, keyed by the whole hash (`name_hash`), each
with the ideas that go by it. A kelve asks for a bucket by prefix and
finds its own name in it, so the graph never learns which name it was
after, as Have I Been Pwned does for passwords.

Candidate.description:
An idea a name may be. The asker's own model chooses among candidates
for what it reads; only the graph decides what it writes.

definition.description:
What it is, in a line: how a model tells two ideas with one name
apart.

match.description:
Whether this is surely the idea: its name or one of its other names
is exactly the one asked for, and no other idea's is.

score.description: From 0 to 1: how alike the names are.

Card.description: What a lesson is matched by.

codes.description: Codes and rule ids of the problems it answers: `E0425`, `ValueError`.

cues.description:
Words or names that show it's relevant where they appear: `thread_rng`,
`\cite{`, "et al.".

holds.description: "Holds when", as conditions kelve can check against the work.

roles.description: The kinds of file it's for: `bibliography`, `test`, `data file`.

tools.description: The commands or tools it's for: `cargo`, `pandoc`, `pytest`.

variants.description:
The problem it answers, as different tools and versions print it,
normalised (`lesson::seen_as`).

oneOf.description: Adds an idea, defined, or finds the one the graph already has.

Writes an idea's entry. Its idea and the ideas its links lead to are
IDs, or `ref:` an idea this changeset adds. Its claims, each with
the numbers of the sources behind it, are for the graph's checks: an
older kelve sends none.

For an idea that has an entry: what this does to it. A fix,
only while the graph's checks have found problems; an extend,
to a sound entry; a rewrite, only when the entry is poor or
mostly wrong (`kelve_core::entry::revise`).

Proposes that one idea relates to another, and why. Both are IDs, or
`ref:` an idea this changeset adds. It's reviewed before anyone sees it.

model.description:
The model that proposed it, by its catalogue ID, so it's reviewed
by others. None when a person proposes it by hand.

rank.description: For "rests on": 1 for the most needed.

why.description: One plain sentence: what `from` takes from `to`.

oneOf.description:
Proposes taking a relation back, and why. The judges review it, as
they would a report.

Change.description:
One change in a changeset. An idea the same changeset adds is referred
to as `ref:` and its `ref` until it has an ID.

Changeset.description: A batch of changes, and what made them.

agent.description: What made it, and its version: `kelve/0.1.0`.

oneOf.description:
The person's agent that wrote what it adds, and the model it ran on,
so one provider's work can be found again if it ever must be.

Checking.description:
How the graph's check of an entry it hasn't served yet stands, for the
account that wrote it.

claims.description: Each claim, by its number from 1, in order.

problem.description: Why it was turned away, when it was, in a sentence.

Claim.description:
A factual statement an entry makes, and the numbers of its sources
that support it: none for what any textbook says.

block.description: The block that makes it, by id, when the writer said.

faulted.description:
Whether it's in a block the graph's checks since found wrong. A
revision is served as it was, so the graph never sets it; kelve
marks it from the idea's `faulted`, for its agent.

key.description:
Its key (`kelve_core::entry::claims::key`), as the graph serves
it: the graph works it out from what's sent.

quotes.description:
The words on each cited page that say it, as the writer copied
them: the graph finds each on its page before it checks the claim.

carried.description:
Carried from an earlier check: the same claim, from the same words
on a page that hasn't changed, so it wasn't judged again.

found.description:
For one that failed: what its pages don't show, or that a quote
isn't on its page. kelve gives it, as it is, to the agent fixing
the claim, with the claim's words and quotes.

CodeNote.description: A note pinned to a line of an annotated excerpt.

line.description: Where the line is among the excerpt's lines, from 0.

Counts.description:
A week of how one kelve was used, as numbers only, which its person chose to
share. It says nothing about who sent it, or what they opened, read or
wrote. Its one ID is the install's, random, made when its person said yes
and gone when they stop: never sent with the graph's key or reading tokens,
so the graph can't tie it to an account.

agent.description: What sent it, and its version: `kelve/0.1.0`.

byDay.description:
The same counts, a day at a time: each day with any use, as
`2026-10-13`, the person's own date.

contributing.description: Whether it adds to the shared graph.

counts.description:
Each count, by what it counts: `opened.change`, `links.followed`,
`links.written`, `entries.read`, `notes.agent`, and so on.

days.description: Days in the week it was used.

deepDays.description: Days on which three or more links were followed.

install.description: The install's ID: 32 hex characters, 128 random bits.

weeksIn.description: Whole weeks since this kelve was first used: 0 in its first week.

Dropped.description: A checked claim a revision leaves out, and why.

Entry.description: An entry: the page for one idea. Every idea has exactly one.

links.description: The terms in its prose that lead on, each to an idea.

minutes.description: About how long it takes to read, in minutes.

question.description:
The one question it answers, as a reader would ask it: the line under
the idea's name. Empty in an entry written before there was one.

title.description: A title that says what it's about, in plain words.

EntryPage.description: An idea's entry, as one revision of it.

claims.description:
Its claims, each with its key and where it's made: what a writer
changing the entry must keep.

reviewed.description: Whether a person has reviewed it, beyond kelve's own checks.

revision.description: This revision, never reused: an entry at a revision never changes.

Facet.description: One condition a lesson holds under.

in.description: On a list axis (a place, a language, a platform, a setting): one of these.

introduced.description: On an ordered axis (a version, an edition, a date): from this one on.

name.description: What it's about on that axis: a package, a style guide, a setting.

Feed.description:
What became public, oldest first, for mirrors: `next` is where to ask
from next time.

kind.description:
`live`: an idea went live. `merged`: a live idea merged `into`
another. `entry`: a `revision` became its idea's entry. `pulled`: its
entry was reverted, back to `revision`, if any. `withdrawn`:
a live idea left the graph. `relation`: a `relation` from `idea`
came to `state`. `split`: a live idea was found to be two, one of
which is `into`; it comes once for each.

Flag.description:
A reader's word that an entry, or one link in it, is wrong. The graph's
models check it again, with nothing that says who sent it.

link.description: A link's term, when it's the link that's wrong.

oneOf.description:
A relation, when it's a relation that's wrong ("this didn't help me
understand"); then `revision` may be empty.

revision.description: The entry's revision, as the reader saw it.

why.description: What's wrong, in the reader's words.

Fold.description: What a fold holds: more than the part says, for the reader who wants it.

Followed.description:
A relation a reader followed: from one idea's entry to the idea it
relates to, by how it relates. Nothing else: no account, no install, no
project, no file, no time.

Follows.description:
Relations followed, sent in a batch at most once an hour, in random
order, without the account's key.

Formula.description:
The formulas an explorable can use. kelve computes them; the model only
picks one and sets its inputs.

Frame.description: One step of a step-through: a caption, and the nodes it marks.

value.description: How many reach it, in any unit, the same for every stage.

Idea.description: An idea: what it is, and whether its entry is written yet.

asks.description:
What its readers, or the graph's own grade, ask its entry to add,
most asked first: only what the graph would take now. A person's
kelve that adds to the graph has its agent extend the entry when
it's opened.

depth.description:
How many steps of served "rests on" it is from a foundation: none
until a chain reaches one. The graph works it out.

faulted.description:
The blocks of that revision those problems are in, by id, as far as
the graph can tell: what a fix may change.

foundation.description:
Whether it's a first principle, on the ground floor: the open list's
word, until three model families change it.

problems.description:
What the graph's checks found wrong with that revision since it was
accepted, in sentences: a reader's report the judge upheld, a claim
its pages no longer support, a page gone. While there are any, a
person's kelve may write the entry again, to replace it.

reads.description: How many times its entry has been read, with nothing about who.

revision.description:
The current revision of its entry, when it has one that's been
accepted.

IdeaAsk.description: What an idea's entry is asked to add.

oneOf.description: The part it goes under, when it's known.

readers.description: How many readers asked: none when it's the graph's own grade.

IdeaRef.description: An idea, as entries, marks and notes point at it.

name.description: The name it goes by: "Advisory locks".

IdeaRelations.description: How one idea relates, both ways: everything served about it.

down.description: What it rests on, most needed first.

grounds.description: The first principles it comes down to, by any way.

Ideas.description:
Ideas asked for by ID: the ones found, IDs that now redirect to another,
IDs of ideas found to be two, and IDs the graph doesn't know.

split.description:
An idea models found to be two ("normalization" for text, and
for probabilities), by its old ID: the IDs of the ideas it is now.
Which one a use of it means is for whoever used it to say.

Instructions.description:
What a person's agent is told to do for one kind of job. The graph serves
them, so they improve for everyone at once.

Lesson.description:
A lesson, as an agent writes it and the graph serves it. `about` is the
graph's IDs once kelve has matched the agent's names.

do.description: What to do about it, as one action.

chance.description:
How likely it was given, in thousandths, at the moment it fitted:
what weighs it when lessons are measured together.

withheld.description:
Held back from the agent, to measure the lessons: what came of the
moment without it. Never counted in the lesson's record.

LessonPage.description: A lesson as the graph serves it: `about` holds the ideas' IDs.

card.description:
What it's matched by, made by the graph from its own words only:
cues, codes, the problem as tools print it, and "holds when" as
conditions (`core::matching`). Empty from a graph that makes none;
kelve then makes its own.

contradicts.description:
The lessons it contradicts, by ID: another good way, each with when it
holds. Both stay; what held ranks them.

given.description:
How many times it was given, across every account, as kelves said what
came of it: a kelve holds a lesson back as a control only once it's
widely used.

id.description: The graph's ID for it, never reused: `kelve:l…`.

record.description: What came of it for projects besides its author's.

why.description: Why it was turned away, when it was.

LessonState.description: Where a lesson is in the graph.

Lessons.description:
The live lessons about some ideas, best first, and where merged ideas
went.

mark.description: The line that matters, marked in red.

n.description: Its line number in the real thing, when it has one.

Link.description:
A term in an entry's prose, written `[[term]]`, and the idea it leads
to. The graph matched the idea; the model only named it.

kind.description: What the link says about it, for the graph; readers see words.

term.description: The words as the prose has them, without the brackets.

LinkKind.description:
What a link in an entry says about the idea it leads to. The person
only ever sees words; this keeps the graph sound.

Manifest.description: What a graph is: its prefix for idea IDs, and what it calls itself.

minClient.description:
The oldest kelve that may use it: an older one asks the person to
update.

space.description: The prefix of every idea ID it mints: `kelve`.

MatchRequest.description: Names to look up, keyed by the asker's own keys.

mark.description: The point that matters, in red.

oneOf.description: The block with this block's id, replaced by it.
A block taken out, and why.
A new block, after the block with the id `after`, or first.

Op.description: One change to an entry's blocks, by id.

Outcome.description: What came of a lesson an agent was given.

Outcomes.description:
What came of lessons an agent was given, sent in a batch, as the
person's account so that one project counts once. Nothing else: never
the problem, the command or the file.

Part.description:
The parts of an entry, in the order they come: an opening that stands
alone, then five parts, each optional but the opening.

Problem.description: An error, as RFC 9457 problem details.

QuadrantAxis.description: An axis of a quadrant: what its low and high ends mean.

x.description: From 0, the low end, to 100, the high end.

Query.description: A name to find ideas for, with a word of where it came up.

context.description:
A word or two of the field it's from: "databases", "React". Never
anything from what the person opened beyond that.

Quote.description:
The words on a page that support a claim, by the entry's number for the
page.

Record.description:
What came of lessons for projects other than its author's, one count a
project, and whether a page backs it.

Rel.description:
A relation from one idea, as readers see it: the idea at its other end,
why, where it stands, and its rank among rests-on.

RelationKind.description: What one idea's tie to another says.

RelationRef.description: One relation, by its ends and kind.

RelationTaken.description: A relation a changeset proposed or took back, and where it stands.

Relations.description:
Relations asked for by idea ID, as `Ideas` is: by each ID found, IDs
that redirect, IDs of ideas found to be two, and IDs the graph doesn't
know.

Revise.description: What an entry written against another revision does to it.

oneOf.description: For an extend: what it was asked to add.

base.description:
The revision it was written against: its idea's current one, as the
writer read it.

dropped.description: The base's checked claims it leaves out, by key, each with why.

ops.description:
For a fix or an extend, what it does, block by block. The entry it
carries is the base with these applied; written against a revision
since replaced, they're applied to the current one when they touch
no block that changed.

RevisionKind.description: What kind of revision it is.

SequenceMessage.description: One arrow in a sequence: from one actor to another, by name.

mark.description: The one that matters, in red.

SignInCode.description:
What a person's kelve sends to sign in, once the graph has sent their
browser back to it: the one-time code it came with, the PKCE verifier
only this kelve holds, and the address the code was sent to.

SignedIn.description:
What it gets for the code: a key of its own, and the name what it adds
is shown with, which the graph makes up.

Source.description:
A source an entry cites: a page kelve fetched from its publisher, or a
session it heard. Numbered as the margin shows them.

archived.description: A copy at the Internet Archive, if kelve made one.

published.description: When it was published, as the page says: "2024".

publisher.description: Who published it, or wrote it: "Docker", "Panickssery, Bowman and Feng".

url.description: Its address, from the publisher; none for a session kelve heard.

at.description: From 0, the low end, to 100, the high end.

Standing.description: How far a lesson is confirmed, as the graph ranks it.

Terms.description: What a person agrees to before anything they add goes into the graph.

points.description: What the screen says, a point at a time.

text.description: The terms in full, as markdown.

Timestamp.description:
A UTC timestamp. It always serialises with milliseconds
(`2026-09-30T12:40:00.000Z`), like JavaScript's `toISOString`, so two of
them compare the same as strings as they do as times.

TokenAsk.description: A batch of blinded tokens to sign, for the key with `id`.

blinded.description: Each blinded token, base64url: at most 100.

TokenGrant.description:
The batch signed: each in the order asked, the proof they were all
signed with the key shown, and how many more the account may have today.

TokenKey.description:
The key the graph signs tokens with, as it shows everyone: its ID, and
the public key a batch's proof is checked against.

id.description: The first eight bytes of the public key's SHA-256, in hex.

TreeBranch.description: A branch of a tree: the question at the top has no parent.

edge.description: The words on the way down to it: "yes", "under 10 people".

parent.description: The branch it comes from, earlier in the list.

values.description: One for each of the trend's labels.

Up.description:
What rests on an idea: how many, and the first of them, most read
first. The rest come a page at a time (`Client::up`).

UpPage.description: A page of what rests on an idea: `next` asks for the page after.

Version.description:
One side of a before and after: lines of the real thing kelve copied
in (with `from`), or lines written to show the idea (without).

lang.description: What it's written in: a language in `code::LANGUAGES`, or none.

WrittenBy.description:
Who wrote what a changeset adds: the person's agent, its model, and its
plan when the agent said.

agent.description: The agent, as it names itself: `claude-code`.

model.description: The model it ran on, as it named it: `claude-opus-5-5`.

token.name: Authorization
token.description: A reading token, spent once: `PrivateToken token=…`.
